item.title: Regional Mediators Rush to Save U.S.-Iran Cease-Fire
item.description: Pakistan and Qatar have dispatched teams to Iran under the looming threat of resumed war, after weeks of diplomacy failed to produce an agreement.

item.title: Middle East live: EU moves to widen sanctions on Iran, threats to freedom of navigation
item.description: The EU Council on Friday said in a statement that it would extend the scope of sanctions targeting Tehran's military support for Russia's war against Ukraine to include individuals and entities involved in Iran's actions to threaten the freedom of navigation in Hormuz. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Top Republican warns Trump against making a deal with Iran: 'Finish the job'
item.description: Sen. Roger Wicker publicly warns Trump against pursuing a weak Iran deal, urging the president to continue military pressure on Tehran's regime.

item.title: Israel far-right finance minister says ICC prosecutor seeks arrest warrant against him
item.description: Israel's far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said on Tuesday the International Criminal Court prosecutor had sought an arrest warrant against him, blaming the Palestinian Authority for the move. Smotrich said Israel would respond by ordering the evacuation of the Palestinian Bedouin community of Khan al-Ahmar in the occupied West Bank.

item.title: Death toll from Israeli strikes on Lebanon passes 3,000, officials say
item.description: It marks a grim milestone in the conflict between Israel and the Lebanese armed group Hezbollah since March, despite a nominal ceasefire.

item.title: Hezbollah support endures in south Lebanon as ceasefire fails to stop war with Israel
item.description: Despite continuing Israeli attacks and occupation, many people in the south still believe the armed group is the only force capable of defending them.

item.title: Israel's Ben-Gvir sees 'no innocent people in Gaza or even Europe': Journalist Gideon Levy
item.description: FRANCE 24's François Picard welcomes veteran Israeli journalist and Haaretz columnist Gideon Levy. He offers a scathing analysis of Israeli politics, the Gaza war, the unprecedented rise of xenophobic nationalism and Israel's growing dependence on the United States. Speaking from Tel Aviv amid mounting electoral tensions, Levy argues that "everything – war and peace, domestic politics, legislation – is now covered by the shadow of the upcoming elections".

item.title: First Gaza flotilla activists deported by Israel arrive in Turkey
item.description: The first group of foreign activists from the Global Sumud aid flotilla arrived in Turkey on Thursday after Israel deported them following global outcry over their treatment in custody. A viral video released Wednesday showed Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir heckling the detained activists as they were bound and kneeling. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Digital bottleneck: How Iran wants to use internet access as leverage in the war
item.description: Tehran is floating the idea of charging the world’s largest tech companies – including Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon – for using the undersea internet cables crossing the Strait of Hormuz in a new attempt to exploit its control over the critical waterway to ratchet up economic pressure on the West.

item.title: Iran ‘prefers diplomacy’ but if there’s a war, Tehran says it’s ready
item.description: Iran and the US traded threats as President Donald Trump warned of renewed strikes a day after he said he held off a major assault in hopes of a peace deal. Reporting from Tehran, FRANCE 24’s Reza Sayah says Iranian officials have maintained their position that “they prefer diplomacy. They don't see a military solution to this conflict,” he explains. “But if there's a war, they're ready for it.”
